Subject: Post-call: SLO targets & concurrency needs (ACME)

Thanks again for the demo earlier — quick recap and a couple of clarifications so we can move to sizing/quote.

Key SLO targets from our side:
- 95th p95 latency goal: <= 350ms for non-streaming text-gen (avg request 500 tokens)
- Streaming responses: low-latency chunked streaming for live UI (target start-of-stream < 150ms)
- Throughput: steady-state 1,200 reqs/min during business hours (peak burst to 2,500 reqs/min for ~10min)
- Concurrency: up to 300 concurrent requests during peak; many of these are short-lived streaming connections (WebSocket/proto-stream)

We attached our current SLO spreadsheet (acme_slo_requirements.xlsx). Questions we have for Redwood:
1) How do your rate limits and concurrency quotas map to these numbers?
2) For streaming, do you count open streaming connections toward concurrency quotas differently?
3) What connection pooling / keepalive behavior do you recommend for our gateway?

Next steps: please send a short note with the mapping to Redwood limits and any recommended config. Happy to jump on a 30m call if helpful.

Thanks,
John
John Doe

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO targets & concurrency needs (ACME)

John — thanks for the clear recap and the spreadsheet, that helps a lot. Below is a concise mapping and a few follow-up clarifying questions so our provisioning team can size Dedicated capacity or propose Hosted limits.

Quick mapping to Redwood quotas (initial thoughts):
- Per-user/request rate limits: Hosted default throttles are per-api-key and per-IP. For your steady 1,200 reqs/min and 2,500 reqs/min burst, we recommend a dedicated quota (reserved capacity) or an increased hosted quota.
- Concurrency: Redwood treats concurrent active request slots separately from open streaming connections. For streaming via our streaming API (chunked HTTP) we count active token-generation calls as concurrency while the model is actively generating; idle open connections (waiting) are tracked but weighted lower. For your use case (300 concurrent active requests with many short streaming sessions) we would size for 350 active slots to allow headroom.
- Connection pooling / keepalive: recommend short-lived pooled connections with HTTP/1.1 keepalive or HTTP/2 multiplexing from your gateway. For WebSocket-style long lived streams, we recommend a per-instance connection pool and a gateway-level circuit breaker to avoid head-of-line resource exhaustion.

Follow-ups we need from you:
- Typical average prompt + completion token lengths (you gave ~500 tokens earlier; please confirm split prompt vs completion)
- % of requests that are streaming vs non-streaming (ballpark)
- Any strict SLA required for 99th percentile latency or sustained throughput windows beyond the stated targets

We attached a short note with Redwood concurrency options (redwood_concurrency_options.pdf) and will draft a formal quota proposal once we have the token split and streaming percentage. If you want, we can schedule a 30m call tomorrow to walk the draft.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood_concurrency_options.pdf

Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. Answers below inline.

- Token split: average prompt ~120 tokens, average completion ~380 tokens (total ~500 tokens)
- Streaming vs non-streaming: roughly 60% streaming (live chat UI), 40% non-streaming (batch responses)
- 99th percentile latency: we'd like 99th <= 800ms for non-streaming; for streaming start-of-stream p99 <= 300ms

A few more details on connection behavior from our infra team:
- We plan to maintain HTTP/2 multiplexing for the majority of traffic from edge to Redwood (preferring fewer connections with many streams).
- For client WebSocket connections (browser->gateway) the gateway will fan-in to fewer long-lived upstream streams; so most streaming sessions will result in short-lived active generation on Redwood but many open client flows.

Let me know if you need sample traffic profiles (we can share a 24h csv or summary). If you can draft a quota + pilot config that includes: reserved concurrency, burst allowances, and streaming multipliers, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
John

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: SLO targets & concurrency needs (ACME) — action: quote + pilot plan

Forwarding ACME's final clarifications. Action items for sizing/quote:
- Use token split prompt=120 / completion=380 and 60% streaming ratio.
- Target: support 1,200 reqs/min steady, 2,500 reqs/min burst, 300 concurrent active requests. Recommend provisioning for 350 active slots to include buffer.
- Propose: Dedicated pilot with a reserved concurrency pool + an elevated hosted quota fallback. Include burst credit for 10-minute peaks (allow +50% burst for 10 minutes) and a streaming multiplier of 0.6 for idle connection crediting (i.e., count idle streams as 0.6 of active slot).
- Prepare two artifacts: 1) customer-facing quota proposal (pdf) and 2) internal sizing notes (internal_sizing_notes.txt).

Please loop in infra if GPU type assumptions matter (likely A10 vs A100 sizing). I'd like a draft by EOD Wednesday so I can share with ACME for pilot approval.

Thanks,
Marissa
